props.title: When will Russia cease active military hostilities against Ukraine?
props.shortTitle: When will Russia end its military aggression?
props.details:
Resolution: The cessation of active military hostilities means the absence of offensive actions by Russian Federation troops, including missile, bomb and drone attacks on targets in Ukraine, with or without an official declaration of a ceasefire, for at least 2 weeks. The question will resolve based on public reports from the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine. The question will resolve for the time period (quarter, semester, etc.) when the cessation of hostilities began.

Background: In the past few months, more and more Western leaders have been making statements indicating their conviction that the war in Ukraine can be ended through diplomatic negotiations. Russia’s demands for such hostilities to end include Ukraine ceding control of five regions (Crimea, Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhia, Kherson) that Russia has unilaterally annexed (including parts currently not controlled by Russia), a significant reduction of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, as well as an agreement by Ukraine not to join NATO. Ukraine, in turn, argues that such a cessation of hostilities will only be used by Russia to prepare for renewed aggression, as happened after the Minsk agreements in 2014-2015.
